sentences.text: Dated : 19-10-2023  Shri Mohammad Ali - Advocate with Shri Ahmad Sajid Hussain - Advocate for the appellants.
Shri O.P. Patel - Panel Lawyer for State.

Heard on I.A.No.15844/2023, which is second application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail filed on behalf of appellants namely,
Gyanbai, Ramadhar Chadhar and Rohit Singh.

Each of the appellants have been convicted for offence punishable under Section 409 read with Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.2000/-, Section 420 read with Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years and fine of Rs.2000/-, Section 467 read with Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.2000/-, Section 468 read with Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 5 years and fine of Rs.2000/- and Section 471 read with Section 120-B of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 2 years and fine of Rs.2000/- respectively, with default stipulations.
Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the appellants are innocent and have falsely been implicated in the matter.
He also submits that the trial Court has not properly appreciated the oral and documentary evidence available on record and committed error in convicting the appellant for aforesaid offence.
Appellants are in custody and appeal would take considerable time to conclude.
They are ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions, which may be imposed by this  2 Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be considered.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.
Heard counsel for the parties and perused the record.
This is repeat application under Section 389(1) of Cr.P.C. filed on behalf of the appellants.
The earlier one was dismissed as withdrawn.

This bail application has been argued on the ground of parity, which the appellants are claiming with co-convict Praveen Asati who was granted the Smt. Gyan Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93545801/
1 benefit of suspension of sentence in CRA No.12703/2022 vide order dated 27.06.2023 .

sentences.text: Co-convict Praveen Asati, was the Sub Engineer, who prepared the measurement book regarding a road which according to prosecution was never constructed.
The appellants are the Sarpanch and Sachiv in whose tenure the alleged construction was made.

Therefore in context of crime committed,
their role cannot be assessed on different parameters from the one applied to Praveen Asati.
Having considered the facts of the case and also that the co-convict Praveen Asati has already been released on bail after suspending his sentence, the I.A.No.15844/2023 is allowed.

I t is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) each with one solvent surety each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned, the custodial sentence of the appellants shall remain suspended and they shall be released on bail for securing their presence before the trial Court concerned on 20.12.2023 and on such other dates as may be fixed in this regard during pendency of this appeal.
Accordingly, the aforesaid I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.
List this case for final hearing alongwith Cr.A. No.12703/2022 in due course.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Date: 2023.10.20 17:06:59 +05'30'
